open_points.subject: A19 — UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES
open_points.question: What exact byte value does `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` have in this release?
options: 65536 bytes
1048576 bytes
another explicitly fixed byte count

witness.initial: An authenticated owner session already holds an import file; a new multipart upload has 131072 bytes before the file part.
events: The owner submits the new upload with the CSRF field first and the file second.
outcomes: An implementation using a 65536-byte head limit refuses the upload and retains the previous file.
An implementation using a 1048576-byte head limit accepts the upload and replaces the previous file.

open_points.subject: A19 — upload-form head limit
open_points.text:
the head read before the file — at most the data provider's
   `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` —
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: The passage must name `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` as the imported constant read by the receiving code.

open_points.subject: A19 — oversized multipart head
open_points.text:
the head read before the file — at most the data provider's
   `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` —
open_points.question: What must Registry do when the file part has not begun by the time this many head bytes have been read, and does that refusal preserve the session's previously uploaded file?
options: Refuse immediately as an unreadable upload and preserve the previous file
Refuse with a distinct oversized-head condition and preserve the previous file
Continue reading while imposing the bound only on retained head bytes
open_points.default_guess: Refuse immediately as an unreadable upload and preserve the previous file

witness.initial: An owner session holds file A; the next multipart request has a valid CSRF value but more than `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` before its file part.
outcomes: Registry stops at the head limit, refuses the upload, and keeps file A.
Registry continues through the oversized head, accepts file B, and replaces file A.

open_points.subject: A19 — accepted multipart shape
open_points.text:
The upload is the file the owner
   interface's form sends as the second part of a multipart body, after the
   field that carries the CSRF value
open_points.question: Is that exact two-part order an acceptance condition, and what happens to multipart requests with the file first, repeated CSRF or file parts, another part between them, or parts after the file?
options: Accept only one CSRF part followed by exactly one final file part
Locate one CSRF part and one file part in any order and refuse duplicates
Use the first matching CSRF and file parts and ignore additional parts
open_points.default_guess: Accept only one CSRF part followed by exactly one final file part

witness.initial: The owner is authenticated and has a valid CSRF value.
events: A client submits a multipart request containing the file first and the valid CSRF field second.
outcomes: Registry refuses the request because the required part order is not met.
Registry locates both named parts, validates the CSRF value, and accepts the file.

open_points.subject: A19 — declared file-part length
open_points.text:
Its declared length is the request's declared length less
   the head read before the file — at most the data provider's
   `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` — and the closing delimiter
open_points.question: Which exact octets constitute the head and closing delimiter, are a multipart preamble or epilogue allowed, and what happens when the declared request length is smaller than those subtracted values or disagrees with the actual framing?
options: Permit only the generated two-part form, define every framing octet, and refuse inconsistent or negative arithmetic as unreadable
Exclude all valid multipart framing, preamble, and epilogue from the file length
Treat an inconsistent declared length as absent and rely on streaming the file part
open_points.default_guess: Permit only the generated two-part form, define every framing octet, and refuse inconsistent or negative arithmetic as unreadable

witness.initial: The file payload is exactly 52428800 bytes and the multipart body has a nonempty epilogue after its closing boundary.
events: The owner submits the body with a request Content-Length that includes the epilogue.
outcomes: Registry excludes the epilogue as multipart framing and accepts the exactly-at-limit file.
Registry subtracts only the named closing delimiter, treats the epilogue bytes as part of the declared file length, and refuses before reading the file.

open_points.subject: A19 — representation counted by the size limit
open_points.text:
the limit and every byte this rule counts are the file part's, never the
   form's framing
open_points.question: Are the counted bytes the raw octets between multipart boundaries or the payload after any multipart content-transfer decoding, and are encoded file parts refused?
options: Count raw file-part body octets and refuse content-transfer encodings
Count decoded file payload bytes
Count both encoded and decoded sizes and enforce the limit on each
open_points.default_guess: Count raw file-part body octets and refuse content-transfer encodings

witness.initial: A multipart file part carries a transfer encoding whose wire body is larger than 52428800 bytes but whose decoded payload is smaller.
events: An authenticated owner submits the upload with a valid CSRF field first.
outcomes: Registry counts the raw part octets and refuses it as oversized.
Registry decodes the part, counts the decoded payload, and accepts it.

open_points.subject: A19 — ordering of CSRF, framing, and size checks
open_points.text:
a declared length over the limit is refused before any byte is
   read
open_points.question: After reading the multipart head but before reading file bytes, in what order must Registry validate multipart structure, validate the CSRF value, enforce the head bound, and refuse an over-limit declared file length when more than one check would fail?
options: Validate framing and CSRF first, then enforce the declared file length
Enforce head and declared-length limits before validating CSRF
Return one indistinguishable refusal while fixing an internal check order
open_points.default_guess: Validate framing and CSRF first, then enforce the declared file length

open_points.subject: A21 — retention of multipart head
open_points.text:
the
head before it is bounded by a constant and never kept
open_points.question: What does “never kept” prohibit: durable or session retention only, retention after the file part begins, or even temporary bounded buffering while parsing and validating CSRF?
options: Temporary bounded buffering is allowed, but the head is discarded immediately after validation and never enters session or durable state
The head may remain in request-local memory until the request completes
No complete head may be buffered at any time
open_points.default_guess: Temporary bounded buffering is allowed, but the head is discarded immediately after validation and never enters session or durable state

witness.initial: A valid upload has a CSRF field and multipart headers before its file part.
events: Registry parses the request and processes the file.
outcomes: Registry buffers the bounded head until validation finishes, then discards it.
Registry streams and discards each head fragment without retaining the complete head.
witness.observer: an implementation-level memory or security check

open_points.subject: A19 — Required tests item 4
open_points.text:
An import file of exactly 50 × 1024 × 1024 bytes, sent by the upload form
   with its CSRF field first, is read; one of a byte more is refused, with
   no mapping shown, also when its declared length is smaller or absent, and
   the file the session kept before stays kept.
open_points.question: What Required tests item must show that an over-limit declared file-part length is refused before any file byte is read, that the multipart head never exceeds `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`, and that an over-limit head is handled as decided?
options: Add an instrumented test proving the early declared-length refusal and a boundary test at and above the head limit
Extend item 4 to state those observations explicitly
Leave those normative properties without a required test
open_points.default_guess: Add an instrumented test proving the early declared-length refusal and a boundary test at and above the head limit
